summary:
Build 6 (eda347d, the blog look) holds up when run. I checked it in real Chrome 158 on this machine, using the project's own tests and scratch-only probes. It did not touch a real deployment or a device, so contact is `code`.

**Tests and rules**
- `go test -count=1 -p 4 ./...` with CHROME_BIN exits 0: 34 packages ok in 55 s.
- Run with -v, the slice's browser tests ran and passed rather than skipping:
  - TestEveryScreenIsDesigned: 20 states x 2 widths x 2 schemes, 6276 texts (lowest 5.01:1), 1352 controls. Every role was met: danger confirm in .remove 176, in .block 104, delete 12.
  - TestReportFrameKeepsItsOwnCanvas: in every case the frame matches the report opened alone. A light #ffffff/#ffffff, B dark #204060/#204060, C dark #121212/#121212.
  - TestThreadFitsPhoneWidth: 244 px at level 5 at 360 px.
  - The shell and forbidden-page tests pass, and Fitness holds all 45 rules.

**Independent mutation (my own, in a scratch copy, deleted afterwards)**
- I set `--text-muted` light to #c9c3b8. TestStylesheetTokens failed at 1.65:1 against a 4.5 bar, and TestEveryScreenIsDesigned failed with 1217 problems. So both the static pair check and the rendered contrast check still bite on the new palette.

**Engine screenshots**
- I opened all 48, as per-screen contact sheets: desktop at half scale, phone at full scale.
- The look reads as designed in both schemes, and the admin screens are now photographed. That was the reason for the last send-back.
- The admin Preview frame is empty in the engine's pictures. A scratch overlay test showed this is a capture artefact, not a product fault. While the frame is offscreen it paints only Canvas (#ffffff or #121212, about 590 edge px). Scrolled into view, it paints the report in both schemes (4279 to 7500 ink px).
- The 403 on the Not allowed page is the intended answer.
- The console errors come from the seed's avatars. The owner's are on avatars.example, which the CSP refuses on purpose. The reader's are on the real GitHub avatar host, which has no DNS here.

**Content and constraints**
- tests/acceptance is unchanged from main, and the CSP is unchanged.
- No template has a `<style>` block or a `style=` attribute.
- Fonts are local system stacks only (system-ui sans, a Charter/Georgia serif, a mono stack), with no url() and no '@'.
- The report iframe keeps its sandbox without allow-scripts.
- The report page gained an author byline. That is a content change against the original brief, but the person's later restart asked for "the author and date", and it pins nothing.

**What I filed as extras (cosmetic, not sent back)**
- On phones, any byline that carries a badge ('Author', 'blocked') wraps, and its date row begins with an orphaned '·'. This also happens with ordinary logins, not only the 39-character one the builder noted.
- Reply and Remove stack as separate rows under each owner comment.
- The signed-in phone header takes three rows (already filed).

**Still open**
- O-017 (Firefox and Safari) stays open. Firefox is not installed, Safari does not exist on Windows, and Edge may not be started here.

**History**
- Builds 4 and 5 changed tests only. They were caused by different stages (validate-slice, then code-review), so this is not a loop.

checks.what: Console errors on every engine screen come from the seed's avatar URLs
checks.command: Select-String internal/testutil 'avatars\.example'; git log -S'avatars.example' -- internal/testutil; read seed.go:41-52
checks.evidence: seed.go:48 (added by this slice's build 4, 571ae37) gives the owner 'https://avatars.example/u/4242?v=4', a host the CSP refuses on purpose ('draws the plain circle and never leaves this machine'). So every screen logs CSP errors and the engine grades it 'poor'. readerUser (seed.go:52) uses the real https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/42, which the CSP allows, so the launcher's browser tries to reach GitHub. That gives ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED here. The product is not at fault. A same-origin 404 avatar, as look_test.go uses, would show the same plain circle with no console noise and no outbound request. Nobody required this.

criteria.criterion: 1. Show every screen in its designed look when the visitor's OS asks for dark (prefers-color-scheme: dark)
criteria.how: TestEveryScreenIsDesigned passes with every state measured in dark through Emulation.setEmulatedMedia, and my muted-token mutation failed it with 1217 problems. All 12 engine screens in dark show the warm dark paper, light ink and mint-pine accent, with no browser-default control.

criteria.criterion: 2. Fit every screen on a phone: 375 CSS px on /admin/reports/<slug> with a 64-hex SHA-256, the 5-column /admin table, the file input and a 39-character login in the header
criteria.how: TestEveryScreenIsDesigned passes. It compares scrollWidth with the requested 375 and asserts innerWidth == 375 under mobile emulation. TestLookProbeSeesTheStylesheetBeforeTheDesign passes, so the probe still flags the pre-slice 600 px overflow. In the engine's 390 px pictures of /admin, /admin/reports/e004-look (SHA-256 wraps inside its card) and /admin/blocked, nothing runs sideways.

criteria.criterion: 3. Confirm a destructive action in two steps with every details element open: Remove and Block on the owner's report page, the admin report page and a populated Blocked users page, and Reply at the depth cap
criteria.how: The look test's -v roles show danger confirm in .remove 176, danger confirm in .block 104, danger summary of .remove 176 and of .block 104, danger delete 12, and accent post reply 312. The engine's s6, s8 and s9 pictures show Remove and Block as danger-coloured summaries.

criteria.criterion: 4. Read a report as its author: the owner signed in on /reports/<slug> and the admin pages, captured as screenshots in both schemes
criteria.how: The look test passes, including the owner screenshot signal-colour assay. Its viewport-only limit is waived as N-255. The engine photographed the owner report page (s9) and /admin, /admin/reports/<slug>, the draft page and Blocked users (s5 to s8) in both schemes and at both widths, and I looked at all of them. The danger tones read as dark red in light and salmon in dark, not pure red.

criteria.criterion: 5. Load the collapse script only where a thread is drawn (empty home, found home, report and branch)
criteria.how: TestStaticThreadScript passes. The look test asserts 1 script tag on the found home, report and branch pages and 0 elsewhere, and it passes.

criteria.criterion: 6. Keep hidden states hidden until they apply (#feedback-sent with and without the fragment; button.toggle re-hidden by Eval)
criteria.how: TestEveryScreenIsDesigned passes. Its probe asserts #feedback-sent draws only under its fragment and that a re-hidden button.toggle reads display none. This was measured by the run, not re-mutated by me.

criteria.criterion: 7. Read a deep thread on a phone (level 5 at 360 px)
criteria.how: TestThreadFitsPhoneWidth logs '244 px at 360 px'. The look test's depth-5 body-width check (at least 240 px) passes. In the engine's phone pictures, the level 5 to 9 bodies wrap inside the page.

criteria.criterion: 8. Report frame equals the report alone: report A, no background and no color-scheme, under light
criteria.how: TestReportFrameKeepsItsOwnCanvas: frame-a light shows #ffffff in the frame and #ffffff alone, with the site #faf8f4 around it.

criteria.criterion: 9. Report frame equals the report alone: report B with its own @media dark background, under dark
criteria.how: TestReportFrameKeepsItsOwnCanvas: frame-b dark shows #204060 in the frame and #204060 alone.

criteria.criterion: 10. Report frame equals the report alone: report C opts into color-scheme light dark with no background, under both schemes
criteria.how: TestReportFrameKeepsItsOwnCanvas: frame-c is #ffffff = #ffffff in light and #121212 = #121212 in dark.

criteria.criterion: 11. Refuse a non-owner at the admin door (empty login and 'octo<b>&cat')
criteria.how: TestForbiddenPageTakesTheShell passes. The engine's s12 pictures show the designed 403 page for @octocat in both schemes and at both widths.

criteria.criterion: 12. Tell the owner an upload was refused (real Chrome POST from the /admin form, noValidate, invalid slug, answered with p.error)
criteria.how: The look test's refused-upload state passes. It submits through Tab.Submit and would Fatalf if p.error[role=alert] were missing, and the full probe then passes on that answer at both widths and in both schemes.

criteria.criterion: 13. Keep the design system in one table (undefined var, a literal outside :root, color-scheme outside :root, a signal-near token, a declared pair below 4.5 or 3.0)
criteria.how: TestStylesheetTokens and TestStylesheetCorpus pass. The planted-fault corpus covers the literal, var, color-scheme and signal shapes. For the pair shape, which has no planted test (N-256, waived), my own mutation (--text-muted light #c9c3b8) made TestStylesheetTokens fail at 1.65:1 against 4.5.

criteria.criterion: 14. Give every page the one shell (a template not opening with page-start or closing with page-end, in either templates directory)
criteria.how: TestEveryPageTakesTheShell and TestShellCheckerSeesEachFault pass. No template carries <style or style= (0 matches in 11 templates).

criteria.criterion: Brief: every reader screen (home and /reports/<slug> with the frame, like count, vote controls, comments and the feedback box with own messages and author replies; show-all; branch), signed in and signed out, shows the designed look
criteria.how: A person runs `go run ./internal/testutil/seeded`, then opens /, /reports/e004-look, /reports and the 'continue this thread' page, both signed out and signed in through the picker's 'Continue as a reader', with Windows set to light and then dark, at desktop width and at a 375 px phone width. Each page must show the warm paper, serif titles and pine links and buttons, with no blue underlined default links, no grey bevelled buttons and no sideways scroll. I looked at the engine's s1 to s4, s10 and s11 pictures and saw that look. The only things I saw are the cosmetic wraps listed under checks.

criteria.criterion: Brief: every /admin screen (admin.html, admin_report.html, admin_blocked.html) and the forbidden page shows the designed look, with tables, destructive buttons and the two-step remove
criteria.how: In the same seeded app, a person signs in through the picker's 'Continue as the owner' and opens /admin, /admin/reports/e004-look (scrolling to the Preview), /admin/reports/e004-draft and /admin/blocked. They then sign in as the reader and open /admin, in light and dark, at desktop and 375 px. Each must show the sidebar admin in the same paper and type, pill status badges, red Remove and Block summaries that open a confirm, the red 'Delete this report permanently' button, and the designed Not allowed page. I looked at s5 to s8 and s12. The empty Preview in those pictures is a capture artefact, measured separately.

obligations.evidence: Only Chrome 158 (CHROME_BIN) exists to drive here. Firefox is not installed (Test-Path False on both Program Files paths), Safari does not exist on Windows, and Edge must not be started. light-dark(), the iframe Canvas substrate and the .avatar::after cover were measured in Chrome only. This is a known limit of this machine, not an ask.

not_reached: Firefox and Safari (O-017): light-dark(), the frame's Canvas substrate and the broken-avatar ::after cover were measured only in Chrome 158.
A real phone: every phone measurement is Chrome mobile emulation (375 px in the tests, 390 px in the engine's pictures), not a device.
Production behind the VPS reverse proxy: whether it alters the CSP or caching headers for site.css (Q-010, Q-007).
A real GitHub avatar loading in the running app. The seed's owner avatar is refused by the CSP on purpose, and the reader's real-host avatar had no DNS here.
The admin Preview frame in the engine's full-page pictures: Chrome does not paint an offscreen sandboxed frame there, so the frame was checked only by my in-process scrolled capture.
The published report's admin page (s6) is capped at 4000 px, so its Replace and Delete sections are not in any picture. Only the draft page (s7) shows them.
There is no pixel assay of owner danger colours below the fold (N-255). I saw them only by eye in the engine's full-page pictures.
